title: Anomalous scaling in redirection networks
summary: In networks that grow by isotropic redirection (IR), a new node selects an initial target node uniformly at random and attaches to a randomly chosen neighbor of the target. The emerging networks exhibit leaf proliferation, in which the number of nonleaves scales sublinearly as $N^μ$ and the degree distribution has an algebraic tail with exponent $1+μ$. To understand these mysterious properties, we introduce a class of models with redirection to leaves whenever possible.
